question: A finance approvals process has changed: purchases above a threshold now need two signatures instead of one. A project's instructions still describe the old single-signature rule. What should the project owner do first?
options: A) Upload the email announcing the change so that Claude can work out the new rule from that announcement itself.
B) Archive the project and rebuild it later once the finance team has finished documenting the change.
C) Update the project instructions to describe the new two-signature rule before the project is used again.
D) Tell colleagues to mention the new rule in their prompts whenever they ask about purchase approvals.
correct_answers: C) Update the project instructions to describe the new two-signature rule before the project is used again.
explanations: This leaves the contradicting instruction in place and asks Claude to reconcile the conflict.
Removing a working project is disproportionate when a single rule needs rewriting.
Correct. Durable direction that contradicts the current process must be corrected at the source, and quickly.
This relies on every person remembering, while the wrong rule stays configured for everyone else.
